# Shared fixtures of wall contract v1

CONTRACT.md (repo root) is the canon. These files are shared by the package
(`@submitator/badges`) and the server (submitator-backend, which vendors them
into `test/fixtures/badge_wall_v1/`). Every id and URL here is synthetic.

## vector.json

The RFC 8032 TEST 1 key (`test-rfc8032-1`), one signed payload with its
envelope, and the RFC 8032 TEST 1 empty-message signature. Both suites verify
it. Never edit it by hand: regenerate it together with the backend copy.

## walls/*.json

```
{ "name": string, "now": ISO 8601 UTC, "project": uuid, "payload": string,
  "expect": { "ok": boolean, "reason"?: string, "ids": (string | null)[], "skipped": number } }
```

- `payload` is the exact payload text (what the signature would cover).
- `now` is the clock to check expiry against.
- `expect.ids` are the ids of the badges the package keeps, in order. `null`
  stands for a kept badge whose malformed `id` was dropped.
- `expect.skipped` counts the badges the package leaves out.
- `expect.reason` (only when `ok` is false) is the package's wall-level reason:
  `payload` (not JSON, or not exactly the five keys with the right types),
  `version`, `project`, `timestamps` (malformed, impossible, or `issuedAt`
  not before `expiresAt`), `lifetime` (over 8 days), `expired`, `limits`
  (over 200 badges).
- `hand-*.json` are hand-written by the package: `node scripts/write-fixtures.mjs`
  builds them from `scripts/fixture-cases.mjs`, and a unit test checks that
  they match. `hand-skips.json` holds one bad badge per badge-level rule; the
  name of each says which rule it breaks.
- Walls generated by the server's tree builder (`bin/rails badge_wall:contract_fixtures`)
  sit next to them, with a `SOURCE` file naming the backend commit.

Package details the server can rely on:

- Root nodes are depth 1; a tree may be 16 levels deep.
- The node limit counts text nodes and elements alike.
- Lengths count characters (code points), not UTF-16 units or bytes.
- Spaces around a style value are dropped, not refused.
- `\s` in the contract's patterns (`^https?://[^\s]`, `url\s*\(` and the
  other style tokens) is JavaScript's: besides ASCII whitespace it matches
  U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000
  and U+FEFF. Ruby's `\s` is ASCII only, so a server check written with it
  lets through badges the package skips. `hand-skips.json` has a no-break
  and an ideographic space after the scheme and before `(`.
- Fixture files escape DEL and every Unicode space (`\u00a0`); the decoded
  strings hold the raw characters.

## envelopes/*.json

```
{ "name": string, "project": uuid, "now": ISO 8601 UTC,
  "publicKeys": { keyId: publicKey }, "body": string,
  "expect": { "ok": boolean, "reason"?: "envelope" | "too_large" | "key" | "signature" | "crypto" } }
```

`body` is the exact response body. They come from `scripts/write-fixtures.mjs`
too, signed with the test key.

Signatures and public keys are canonical base64url (RFC 4648 section 3.5):
the unused low bits of the last character are zero. CONTRACT.md does not say
so; the package requires it, and refuses a non-canonical signature with
`envelope` (`signature-non-canonical.json`), although a lenient decoder gets
the same 64 bytes from it. Decode strictly when you run these files (Ruby's
`Base64.urlsafe_decode64` does; `unpack1("m")` does not), or check that
encoding the bytes again gives back the same text.

## rendered/*.html

`wallToHtml` output for every accepted wall that has badges:
`<wall name>.marquee.html` and `<wall name>.row.html`, each followed by one
newline (a wall with fewer than 3 badges renders as a row either way). The
root's `data-sbm-wall` attribute holds the package version; here it reads
`VERSION`, so the files stay the same from one release to the next. The
package writes them (`npx vitest run -u test/unit/html.test.ts`) and checks
them on every run. The server's `BadgeMarker`, `BadgeChecker` and
`DirectoryBadgeChecker` must find the self badge and every directory host
outside `span.sbm-cb` in them.

## pages/*.html

The homepage of every example app in `examples/`, byte for byte as its server
sent it: real framework output (Next.js App Router, Cache Components and Pages
Router, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro on demand and static, plain Node.js), scripts
and hydration data included, which is what the server's checks meet on
customer sites. `node examples/run-example.mjs <app> --save-page` writes one;
CI builds all of them on every run and uploads them as the `contract-v1-pages`
artifact.

Every app renders the good wall of the mock wall server
(`examples/mock-wall-server/`). `pages/manifest.json` says what to expect:

- `project`: the project id (synthetic) of every page;
- `directoryHosts`: the hosts of the directory badges. `DirectoryBadgeChecker`
  must find each of them outside `span.sbm-cb`;
- `customHosts`: the hosts of the custom badges, which sit only inside
  `span.sbm-cb`;
- `pages.<app>.badge`: `found` when the server HTML holds the wall
  (`BadgeMarker` and `BadgeChecker` find the self badge, the self-check of
  CONTRACT.md section 10 counts 1 or more), `missing` for the two client-only
  apps (the wall only travels in the page data, with `?ref=<project>`, so
  `BadgeChecker` must report the badge missing and the self-check counts 0).

The root's `data-sbm-wall` holds the package version the page was built with.
